title: Code work
summary: The bar for anything that changes code in the repo: fixes, features, refactors.

labels.1: Does not clear the bar. Claim is unsupported or the change is wrong.
labels.2: Something real is there, but a reviewer has to redo the verification.
labels.3: Works, and is honestly reported. Thin somewhere.
labels.5: Anchor quality. Root cause named and proven, minimal diff, evidence a stranger could re-run.

pass.note: One dimension below 3 fails the whole claim regardless of the mean.

dimensions.name: Root cause, not symptom
dimensions.five: Names the actual mechanism — file, function, why it fails — and proves it, including disproving a plausible wrong theory when one was in play.
dimensions.one: Describes the symptom, or repeats the theory it was handed without testing it. Catches or suppresses the error instead of removing the cause.

dimensions.name: Evidence a stranger could re-run
dimensions.five: States the exact commands and their real output. Verification touches the thing that actually ships. Failures are shown, not summarised.
dimensions.one: Asserts success. No command, no output, or output from something other than what shipped.

dimensions.name: Only what was asked
dimensions.five: Diff is the smallest change that fixes it. Anything extra found is reported, not silently done.
dimensions.one: Unrelated edits, drive-by refactors, or files touched that the job never mentioned.

dimensions.name: Behaviour when things go wrong
dimensions.five: Bad input degrades safely and visibly. No new crash path. Risky calls are guarded on a real precondition rather than wrapped in a catch.
dimensions.one: Happy path only, or an exception swallowed so the failure becomes silent.

dimensions.name: Reads like the code around it
dimensions.five: Matches local idiom and comment density. Comments explain why, especially where the code looks surprising.
dimensions.one: Foreign style, commented-out code, or comments that restate what the line already says.

references.why: Disproved the briefed root cause with a runnable experiment, named the real mechanism, fixed the cause rather than catching the exception, and verified the shipped artifact.
Correct fix, honestly reported, but verification stopped at 'it compiles' and never exercised the failure it claims to fix.
Claim asserts success with no command output, and the crash is silenced with a catch instead of removed.
